question.problem:
A function $F(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(x)$ | $3.5$ | $8.7$ | $11.2$ | $12.9$ | $6.7$ | $1.2$ |

Approximate ${F}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=2$ using a forward difference approximation.
question.worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation formula

$$
{F}^{′}(x)≈\frac{F(x+h)-F(x)}{h}
$$

 
at the point $x=2.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(2) & ≈\frac{F(2+2)-F(2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{F(4)-F(2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{11.2-8.7}{2} \\  & =\frac{2.5}{2} \\  & =1.25.\end{aligned}
$$
